Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Pinnacle Financial Services Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Pinnacle Financial Services' results for the third quarter. With me this morning are James Whitaker, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Credit Officer; David Kwon, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Ellis, Chief Operating Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Marketing Officer; and Thomas Hale, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to James Whitaker.

James Whitaker:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Pinnacle Financial Services delivered record results in the third quarter, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on sustaining strong revenue growth, driving operational efficiency, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand reputation, promoting a diverse and inclusive culture, and delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our progress. First, our revenue diversification initiatives have significantly bolstered resilience, with non-interest income now comprising 48% of total revenue, up sharply from prior years, driven by robust growth in wealth management, transaction services, investment banking, and consumer fees across regions. Second, credit quality metrics show continued strength, with the NPL ratio at 98 basis points, down notably year-over-year, alongside controlled delinquencies and charge-offs, thanks to proactive underwriting and tech-enabled early warnings. Third, our efficiency ratio improved to 54.2%, reflecting substantial progress through cost optimization, digital shifts, and automation, positioning us ahead of peers. Fourth, net interest income and earnings guidance for next quarter points to sequential growth, with NII expected between $2.58 billion and $2.68 billion amid balanced loan and deposit expansion. Fifth, deposit growth reached 8.2% year-over-year to $285 billion, with a favorable mix shift toward transactional and savings accounts, supported by dynamic pricing and digital tools. Sixth, key strategic initiatives advanced across digital acceleration, client-centric growth, sustainable finance, and operational resilience, yielding strong adoption metrics and fee income gains. Seventh, technology investments have markedly boosted efficiency, with cloud migrations, RPA, and AI delivering hundreds of millions in savings and superior productivity. Eighth, operating expenses trended up modestly at 7.2% year-over-year to $2.48 billion, driven by compensation and tech but offset by procurement and optimization efforts.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, James, and good morning. Pinnacle Financial Services reported net income of $1.5 billion for the third quarter, or $1.48 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 8%, driven by growth in our loan portfolio and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was up 22%, reflecting strong performance in our investment banking and wealth management businesses. We are generating strong returns on equity and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.

Let me expand on several of these areas. Regarding our revenue diversification initiatives, which form a cornerstone of our multi-year transformation, we've pivoted aggressively from an NII-dominant model to fee-based, high-margin streams amid volatile rates, digital shifts, and regulatory changes like Basel IV. Total revenue hit $14.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with non-interest income surging 22% to $6.8 billion, now 48% of the total—up from 38% two years ago and well above our 2020 peak of 72% NII reliance. This buffered the recent 15 basis point Fed cut, with NII at $7.4 billion, benefiting from a 22% deposit beta and NIM at 3.45%, outperforming peers.

In wealth and asset management, AUM expanded 18% to $1.4 trillion on $45 billion inflows, powered by Pinnacle Wealth 360's AI-robo-advisory fused with fiduciary services for mass-affluent clients starting at $250,000 minimums, akin to BlackRock's Aladdin but customized. Fees reached $2.1 billion, up 25%, margins at 42% post-AWS migration, with ESG mandates grabbing 30% of inflows in the booming green bond market. APAC drove 22% growth via Singapore, adding 15,000 HNWIs through Temasek ETF partnerships.

Transaction services and payments exploded 28% to $2.4 billion on $1.8 trillion volumes, via Pinnacle PayFlow's ISO 20022 real-time APIs mirroring JPMorgan's evolution, tapping the $120 trillion B2B market at 7% CAGR per McKinsey. Treasury tools like virtual accounts and blockchain trade finance hit 35% SME adoption, 42% cross-sell in commercial banking, EMEA up 40% post-Brexit via Dublin PSD3 compliance, margins at 55%.

Investment banking added $1.2 billion, up 16%, with ECM/DCM fees up 20% on $45 billion issuances, strong in LevFin amid $1.7 trillion private credit per Preqin, Goldman tie-up for middle-market, and hedged fixed income trading. Consumer cards and digital banking fees rose 19% to $1.1 billion on 4.5 million new accounts, 25% interchange growth from Pinnacle Rewards Visa Infinite, plus $300 million BNPL via Affirm-like partners.

Regionally, North America at 65% grew 15%, APAC 20% exploded 35% on digital wallets, EMEA 12% on IB, LatAm 10% on remittances. Revenue volatility dropped 40%, ROE to 14.2%, with non-interest targeting 52% mix by 2025 at $30 billion annually via $500 million GenAI and quantum payments capex.

On deposits, our franchise grew total deposits 8.2% year-over-year to $285 billion, 11 straight quarters of organic gains outpacing FDIC industry averages, QoQ up 1.5% or $4.1 billion in consumer/SMB. Core ex-brokered grew 6.9%, betas at 35% below peers, cutting FHLB by 22% to $12 billion, HQLA at $95 billion for 115% LCR.

Transactional (DDAs, NOWs, MMDAs) at 42% or $120 billion up 7.1%, DDA 3.2% to $48 billion offset by commercial treasury share gains like JPM, digital app driving 68% usage, balances up 12% to $22,000/user; U.S. Southeast/Texas 9%. Savings at 35% or $100 billion up 10.4%, tiered to 4.75% APY competing with Ally/Marcus, rollovers/emergency funds; PNW 14%, Midwest 11%. Time deposits at 23% or $65 billion up 18.7%, CDs at 4.85-5.10%, brokered capped at 12%; U.S. Florida/California 22%, APAC 15%. Blended cost up 120 bps to 2.45%, top 20 at 4%, uninsured 28% post-SVB sweeps.

Strategies include dynamic pricing engines, UniBank One AI coaches shifting 30% internally, embedded via Plaid/MX for gig workers, deposit centers in branches, 85% C-suite treasury cross-sell. Outlook: 6-8% growth, NIM to 3.55% Q4.

Turning to efficiency ratio, we hit 54.2%, down 210 bps QoQ from 56.3%, 580 bps YoY from 60.0%, best since pre-pandemic, TTM 55.7% toward 55% FY guide, better than JPM 52.8%, BofA 57.1%, Wells 58.4%. Expenses at $2.45 billion up 1.2% YoY via $450 million program 85% complete: 45 branches to digital, 15% back-office cuts via attrition/RPA automating 65% mortgage servicing for $120 million savings.

Revenue up 8.7% to $4.52 billion, NIM +12 bps to 3.45%, non-interest +14%. Consumer/business 52.1% via Mobile 2.0 Zelle/Apple/AI lending, CAC down 22%, digital loans 68%; commercial 56.4% STP 92% trade finance +$85 million fees; wealth 49.8% alternatives/ESG. U.S. 53.1% digital NPS 78; Europe 57.9% Revolut embedded €150 million; APAC 51.7% AWS slashing costs 40%, Grab/Tencent APIs.

nCino Phase 2 95% automation cycle -60%, Temenos AI fraud -35% $60 million save, GenAI CS 45% Tier 1. $1.2 billion 3-year roadmap for 20-25% leverage. FY24 55%, Q4 53.5%, 52% 2025, 48% 2027 with 6-8% revenue CAGR, M&A integration.

For NII and Q4 guidance, Q3 NII $2.52 billion up 4.2% YoY 1.8% QoQ, NIM 3.42% +5 bps QoQ -12 bps YoY despite inversion. Loans +$18.7 billion 7.1% ann., C&I 9.2% Southeast healthcare/manufacturing, consumer 4.8% auto/HELOC. Deposits +$12.4 billion 5.2%, DDA 28%, time beta 4.65% total 62%. $4.2 billion securities swap MBS to SOFR notes +8 bps NIM, FIS/nCino dynamic pricing 85% adjustable.

Southeast 65% loans NII +6.1%, Texas Lone Star +$180 million +25 bps. APAC dip offset RMB deposits. Challenges: MMFs drew $2 billion brokered, countered by Rewards 94% retention, FHLB SOFR+12.

Q4 NII $2.58-2.68 billion 2-6% seq., NIM 3.40-3.50% assuming Dec 25 bps cut, 10yr 4.05%, loans 4-6% ann., deposits 3-5%, betas 60-65%. EPS $1.52-1.62 vs $1.48, expenses $1.85 billion eff. ~56%, non-int $1.12 billion +12% cap mkts/treasury, prov $220 million NPL 0.85%, CECL 1.15%, CET1 11.4%, $1.2 billion buybacks 10% div hike.

Diversifying NII 72% via BNPL Affirm $500 million, Palantir deposit pricing, ROE 14.5% 2025.

Operating expenses at $2.48 billion up 7.2% YoY flat QoQ, low end 7-9% guide, eff. 54.8% from 57.2% YoY 55.9% Q2. Revenue +12% outpacing.

Compensation/benefits $1.11 billion 45% +9.5%, FTE +1.2% to 48,500 salaries +6.8% tech/risk talent vs fintechs, variable -2%. Tech/data $546 million 22% +12%: $180 million AWS/Google core modern, mainframe -15%, $95 million GenAI Palantir/Snowflake fraud/lending, cyber $65 million zero-trust NYDFS. Prof fees $298 million 12% +15%: $45 million CECL/DFAST, $30 million Visa tokenization. Occupancy/equip/marketing $372 million 15%: occupancy flat 45 closures -8% sq ft, marketing +10% $110 million high-yield savings +750K accounts. Other $149 million +4% FDIC $22 million.

North America 75% +8.5% wage/branch opti $25 million save; Europe 15% +5% DORA €35 million UK robo; APAC 10% +3% UPI -18% unit costs +30% deposits. Q4 $2.55-2.60 billion 6-8% FY ~7.5%, AI/Finastra 10-15% payments cuts, $500 million repurchase CET1 11.2%.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, John. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, cybersecurity threats, geopolitical tensions, and regulatory changes like Basel IV. We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

Lisa Patel:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with NPL ratio at 98 basis points, down 12 bps QoQ and 22 bps YoY to lowest since 2019, delinquencies 30-89 days at 2.45% down 25 bps QoQ 55 bps YoY, net charge-offs $142 million or 13 bps ann. down 10% YoY, recoveries 45% up from 38% via collections like JPM.

Consumer 35% book NPL 1.15% up slightly auto sensitive 8.5% prime, NCO 2.1% -15% YoY FICO 680 min; C&I 40% NPL 65 bps NCO 5 bps investment-grade; CRE NPL 1.85% up Sunbelt office/multifamily, NCO 45 bps, $2.3 billion classified +20% QoQ TDR 50 bps concessions, coverage 185% vs peer 120%.

U.S. 75% NPL 0.90% unemp 4.1%; Europe 15% UK delinq -30 bps 2.1%, German C&I <50 bps; APAC 10% China developer 2.2% de-risked 40% HSBC-like. $150 million tech: AI EWS TransUnion/Equifax flags 85% early +28% workouts, CECL recalib +$250 million ALLL 1.45% 145% NPL. Diversify prime unsecured +15% 1.2% NPL, cap CRE office 5%, $1 billion green lending 4.5%. Forward NPL trough H2 90-95 bps, NCO 12-15 bps.

David Kwon:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in cloud migration and AI/ML have yielded significant results, with $1.2 billion Q3 spend unlocking $250 million savings, RPA automating 65% back-office for $180 million FTE equiv., chatbots 72% Tier 1 res., ML fraud 99.2% preventing $450 million losses.

85% workloads multi-cloud AWS/Azure, trans costs -28% to $0.10 handling 2.8 billion digital, productivity 145k txns/FTE +18%. North Am app 18 million MAUs digital dep +40% cost-serve $1.85; Europe PSD2 150+ APIs ComplyAdvantage +14% fees; APAC Razorpay/GCash 90% SME lending -7 to 2hr eff. 52%. GenAI pilots +25% cross-sell, $300 million cyber zero-trust quantum, FY24 capex $4.8-5.2 billion 60% tech blockchain Ripple edge treasury, 1,200 data hires, Plaid/Stripe, $1 billion savings YE25 ROE 16.5%.

Robert Ellis:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making, aligning with our four pillars of digital acceleration, client growth, sustainable finance, and resilience.

Emily Vargas:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention, particularly around high-yield products and digital onboarding.

Thomas Hale:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements, including DORA and NYDFS.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with KBW. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on revenue diversification initiatives and impact?

James Whitaker:
Good morning, John. Happy to elaborate. Our diversification has transformed our top line, with non-interest now 48% of $14.2 billion total up 12%, NII $7.4 billion stable. Wealth AUM $1.4T +18% $45B inflows Pinnacle Wealth 360 AI/human, ESG 30%, APAC Singapore 15k HNWIs Temasek. Payments $2.4B +28% $1.8T vols PayFlow ISO RTP B2B $120T, 35% SME 42% cross-sell EMEA +40%, margins 55%. IB $1.2B +16% $45B issuances LevFin Goldman, cards $1.1B +19% 4.5M accts BNPL $300M. Regional balance, volatility -40%, ROE 14.2%, target 52% mix $30B 2025 $500M tech. This de-risks and outperforms.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mary Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mary Johnson:
What is your outlook for NII and earnings next quarter?

John Ramirez:
Thanks, Mary. Q4 NII $2.58-2.68B 2-6% seq. NIM 3.40-3.50% post Dec cut, loans 4-6% ann. C&I seasonal CRE tight, dep 3-5% betas 60-65%. EPS $1.52-1.62, exp $1.85B eff 56%, non-int $1.12B +12% fees, prov $220M. CET1 11.4% buybacks div +10%. Diversify BNPL Palantir ROE 14.5% 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Can you discuss the impact of credit quality trends?

Michael Chen:
Absolutely, David. Credit remains fortress-like on $450B loans higher rates post-525 bps hikes. NPL 98bps -12 QoQ -22 YoY, delinq 2.45% -25bps, NCO 13bps -10% YoY recov 45%. Consumer NPL 1.15% NCO 2.1%-15%, C&I 65bps, CRE 1.85% coverage 185%. Regional U.S. 0.90%, Europe stable, APAC de-risked. AI EWS +28% workouts CECL 1.45%, outlook trough 90-95bps NCO 12-15bps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
What are your plans for technology investments?

David Kwon:
Great question, Sarah. $1.2B Q3 12% op ex for 15-20% lift, eff 56.2% -420bps. Cloud 85% $250M save trans -28%, RPA 65% $180M, AI chat 72% fraud 99.2% $450M prevented. Regional NA app +40% dep, Europe APIs +14%, APAC 90% lending. GenAI +25% cross-sell cyber $300M, capex $4.8-5.2B blockchain edge 1,200 hires Plaid $1B save ROE 16.5%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to James Whitaker for any closing remarks.

James Whitaker:
Thank you for your interest in Pinnacle Financial Services. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
